prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2019 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim
- Urgent response to the climate and ecological emergency, coupled with deep social and democratic reform. Target: net-zero UK emissions by 2030 via a Green New Deal (GND), investing £100+ billion per year, plus Universal Basic Income (UBI).

Green New Deal priorities
- Energy: Rapid shift from fossil fuels and nuclear to renewables; wind to supply ~70% of electricity by 2030; support for solar, tidal, hydro; community energy; grid/storage expansion; carbon tax rising over a decade; ban fracking; oppose new nuclear.
- Housing: Insulate every home; deep retrofit 1 million homes/year; 10 million homes with rooftop renewables by 2030; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard council homes/year; higher building standards; planning for car‑free living.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than car use; reopen/electrify rail; shift freight to rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycling/walking; end sale of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030; national EV charging; stop new runways and road capacity; Frequent Flyer Levy; ban flight ads; cancel HS2 and road‑building, reinvest in regional rail.
- Industry: Green jobs and training (£2bn/year); decarbonise manufacturing; circular economy; right to repair; 10‑year warranties; ban most single‑use plastics; CCS for cement/steel.
- Food, farming & forestry: 10‑year transition to agroecology; redirect subsidies; cut pesticide use by 50%+; plant 700m trees; rewilding; protect soils/rivers; clearer food labelling; phase‑in meat/dairy tax over 10 years with revenues recycled to farmers; right to food; nature‑based flood management.

Income security
- Universal Basic Income phased in: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disabled people, lone parents, and children; retain Housing Benefit where needed; funded in part by carbon tax.

Democracy and government reform
- People’s Vote on Brexit; campaign to remain and reform the EU (more democratic, transparent, social and environmental standards, freedom of movement).
- Replace First Past the Post with proportional representation; elected second chamber; votes at 16; citizens’ assemblies; Digital Bill of Rights; stronger media plurality rules.
- New Carbon Chancellor with annual carbon budgets; Future Generations Act; scrap Home Office—create Ministries for Sanctuary and Interior; reorient defence to peace and climate security; end arms export promotion.

Public services and rights
- NHS: +£6bn/year rising to 2030; end internal market/privatisation; community health centres; parity for mental health; free contraception; NHS PrEP.
- Education: +£4bn/year for schools; smaller classes; end high‑stakes testing/Ofsted; schools back under local control; free higher education; write off £9k‑era student debt; expand adult education; Climate Education Act and Nature GCSE.
- Nature: Stronger protections; new Environmental Protection Commission; Clean Air Act; right to roam; at least 30% of UK waters fully protected by 2030; urban greening.
- Equality/justice: End hostile environment; humane immigration with right to work for asylum seekers; misogyny a hate crime; fund refuges/Rape Crisis; LGBTIQA+ inclusive PSHE and gender recognition reform; embed UN disability rights; halve prison population via prevention/restorative justice; invest in youth services.
- Drugs: Replace prohibition with regulated, health‑led system; prescription heroin; legal regulated cannabis; evidence‑based access to psychedelics/stimulants; independent drug safety council.
- Animals: Enshrine sentience; ban hunting/snaring; end badger cull; curb animal testing; end live exports; ban cages; method‑of‑production labelling; Commission on Animal Protection.

Tax, spend and funding
- Carbon Tax; merge major personal taxes into a single Consolidated Income Tax taxing income from wealth like work; Corporation Tax to 24%; independent HMRC; clamp down on avoidance/evasion; Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax/Business Rates over 10 years; support small business (mutual banks, prompt payment, SME share of contracts).
- End wasteful projects: cancel Trident, HS2, airport expansion, and road‑building; end NHS internal market, Help to Buy.
- Finance: ~£141.5bn/year operational spend funded by tax reforms and savings; ~£94.4bn/year capital investment via borrowing; public investment to leverage ~£50bn/year private investment.
